# DELETE the dormant inbound absence-probe port

**Decision (operator ruling, recorded on this ticket): DELETE.** This ticket is no longer
an open delete-vs-re-home question; it executes the deletion. Option 2 (re-home the port
to `binding_walk`) is a REJECTED alternative, retained below only so the rejection is
legible.

## What is being deleted, and why it is safe

Bug `3b5f-1b21-ee14-4bdf` removed every consumer of the `(inbound, probe)` chain — the
producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm
`_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, and `reconcile_helpers.route_inbound_probe`. What
remained is a capability with **zero callers**:

* `_backend.SupportsAbsenceProbe` (Protocol) and the three `probe_remote` implementations
  (`adapters/jira/backend.py`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`,
  `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`)
* the neutral vocabulary module `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeBranch`, `ProbeResult`,
  `ProbeConfigError`)
* the Cloud probe `adapters/jira/probe.py` and the shared classifier
  `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` (`classify_probe_response`), whose only callers are the
  `probe_remote` implementations above

This is a **pure deletion with no behavior change**: nothing in a reconcile pass reaches
any of it. Deletion detection is NOT affected — it lives OUTBOUND, in
`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` + `binding_walk`, and the separate **outbound** probe
leaf (`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)` dispatch arm) is live and is NOT
touched by this ticket.

## Why option 2 (re-home to `binding_walk`) is rejected

* The port must NOT be used to restore same-pass re-creation — an earlier operator ruling
  on `3b5f` is that a confirmed-deleted issue is never resurrected. That removes the
  port's original purpose.
* Its stated motivation was false: `binding_walk` already takes the direct-GET as an
  INJECTED `probe_get: Callable`, with `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` as a lazy default
  only — there is no hardcoded private reach for the port to fix.
* It would re-cross an ownership boundary ADR 0028 deliberately draws: absence-vs-deletion
  discrimination is OUTBOUND-owned. Re-homing an INBOUND port there re-splits what `3b5f`
  just consolidated.
* The vocabularies are incompatible in an unsafe direction: `ProbeBranch` has no
  confirmed-404 branch, and its `ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED` conflates deletion with a
  still-alive MOVE — routing it to `binding_walk`'s tombstone could tombstone a live
  moved issue.

## Explicitly OUT of scope (follow-up, not this change)

Deleting the classifier orphans the operator-facing `jira.resolved_statuses` /
`reconciler.resolved_statuses` config keys and the DC transport's `_resolved_statuses`
plumbing. Removing DOCUMENTED config keys is a user-visible surface change needing its own
deprecate-vs-remove decision, so it is deliberately deferred to a follow-up ticket linked
`discovered_from` this one — the same reasoning by which `3b5f` deferred this ticket. The
keys keep their current behavior here (they simply have no reader), so this change stays
behavior-neutral.

## Every file that must change (the deletion's full blast radius)

**Source — deleted outright:** `rebar_reconciler/inbound_probe.py`,
`adapters/jira/probe.py`, `adapters/jira_family/probe.py`.

**Source — edited:** `_backend.py` (drop `SupportsAbsenceProbe`),
`adapters/jira/backend.py` + `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (drop `probe_remote`),
`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (drop `probe_remote` + the classifier import),
`adapters/jira_family/__init__.py` (drop `classify_probe_response` from the imports,
`__all__` and the docstring), `reconcile_helpers.py` (stale docstring),
`adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py` (comment reference), `pyproject.toml` (comment
reference).

**Tests — deleted outright** (they exist only to exercise the deleted units):
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_resolved_statuses_config.py`.

**Tests — edited** (they import or assert the deleted units and would hard-break):
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` (the `probe_remote` stub),
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py`
(`test_classify_probe_response_pins_every_branch`, the `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES` pin),
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_backend_characterization.py` (the DC probe
characterization block and its mutation-log comments),
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`
(`SupportsAbsenceProbe` isinstance + `probe_remote` delegation),
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` (the probe-based
`resolved_statuses` assertion),
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_seam.py` (the `classify_probe_response`
seam tests),
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py` (the live `probe_remote` test).

**Tests — edited because they pin the deleted units BY NAME as invariants** (these fail as
assertions, not merely as imports, so they are called out separately):
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py` (`inbound_probe.py` is an entry
in `_ZERO_ADAPTER_IMPORT_SCALAR_CORE`) and
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` (its boundary example
string names `from rebar_reconciler.inbound_probe import ProbeBranch`).

**Docs:** ADR 0028 (dormant-port Consequences), ADR 0035 (module list), ADR 0055 (shared
probe-classifier unit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] no live caller of the port remains, proven by a Serena semantic search AND
      independently by a plain string grep (per AGENTS.md an empty semantic result alone is
      not trustworthy)
- [x] that proof is recorded as a comment on this ticket
- [x] `SupportsAbsenceProbe` and all three `probe_remote` implementations are deleted
- [x] `inbound_probe.py`, `adapters/jira/probe.py` and `adapters/jira_family/probe.py` are
      deleted, and `classify_probe_response` is dropped from the `jira_family` package
      exports
- [x] the **outbound** probe leaf (`_apply_outbound_probe`, the `(outbound, probe)`
      dispatch arm) is untouched, proven by the existing suite staying green
- [x] epic `e369`'s AC5 is amended to drop the probe classifier from its "one shared
      implementation imported by both backends" clause, with the amendment recorded on
      `e369` and this ticket linked to it
- [x] the dormancy notes in `inbound_probe.py`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe` and ADR 0028 are
      removed along with the code they describe, and ADR 0035 / ADR 0055 no longer list
      the deleted units as shared
- [x] the stale `reconcile_helpers.py` docstring claim that it by-path loads
      `inbound_probe.py` is corrected (no such runtime load exists)
- [x] a follow-up ticket for the orphaned `resolved_statuses` config keys is filed and
      linked `discovered_from` this ticket
- [x] every test file listed above is deleted or updated, so no test imports or asserts a
      deleted unit
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` are green in the worktree
- [x] the change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit before the ticket is closed

## Execution record (2026-08-12)

Landed as Gerrit change 1645, merged to `main` as `b95c097fd4` (`LLM-Review +1`,
`Verified +1`). 30 files, +79 / -1040.

Two deviations from the plan text above, both recorded in comments rather than silently
absorbed:

1. **ADR 0035 is now `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`** — renumbered since
   this plan was written. Same file, same edit.
2. **The config-read gate (`scripts/check_config_reads.py`) turned the deferred
   `resolved_statuses` orphan into a hard CI blocker**, because deleting the classifier left
   `JiraConfig.resolved_statuses` with no attribute-read site. The key was NOT removed — that
   is the user-visible change this ticket defers. Instead the field carries the gate's own
   sanctioned ticket-pointing `# read-via:` marker (reported, never an error; expires when its
   ticket closes) parked against follow-up `549c-032f-6cb0-4258`, and the gate's companion
   invariant test is amended to pin EXACTLY one such marker. `docs/config.md` and
   `docs/user-guide.md` are corrected too: both still promised classification behavior the key
   no longer has. This added `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`,
   `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_heldout.py`, `docs/config.md` and
   `docs/user-guide.md` to the blast radius; `file_impact` is updated to the actual 30 files.

On AC1: both halves of the proof exist on this ticket, but they were run in DIFFERENT
sessions — the Serena semantic search in the earlier session, the string grep in the
executing session. A correction comment records that provenance explicitly rather than
letting the execution comment's overstatement stand.
